description: Create VRM-compatible humanoid skeleton using trimesh with distance-based skinning weights. Export rigged mesh as GLB with skin (joints, inverseBindMatrices).
steps: Add create_humanoid_skeleton() - define bone hierarchy with positions from mesh bounds
Compute bone positions: hips(centroid-0.3Y), spine(+0.1Y), chest(+0.12Y), neck(+0.05Y), head(+0.06Y), eyes(+/-0.03X, +0.02Y, +0.05Z from head)
Add compute_skin_weights() - distance-based weights, normalize to sum=1, max 4 influences
Update rig_avatar() to create skeleton, compute weights, export GLB with skin
Include joints array and inverseBindMatrices in glTF skin
acceptance_criteria: rig_avatar() creates valid GLB with skeleton
GLB contains skins array with joints and inverseBindMatrices
Joint names match VRM humanoid bone names (hips, spine, chest, neck, head, leftEye, rightEye)
verification: python -c "from vtuber_pipeline.avatar.rigging import rig_avatar; result = rig_avatar('assets/canonical_vtuber/template.glb', 'test_rigged.glb'); print(f'Rigged: {result}')"
findings: Implemented create_humanoid_skeleton() with 24 VRM humanoid bones, compute_skin_weights() with distance-based weights and max 4 influences. Added pygltflib dependency for glTF skin export. All acceptance criteria met: GLB contains skins array with joints and inverseBindMatrices, joint names match VRM humanoid bone names, all vertices have skin weights.
